review.research_prompt: Propose drug candidates for human ABL1 and identify which need liver-safety follow-up.

explain.text:
The completed screen of 20 GenMol proposals against human ABL1 yielded 2 candidates flagged for liver-safety follow-up: GEN_e391ee141e35ca355275c63f (rank 1) and GEN_1be062b8a72206ea06c140aa (rank 2). Both received a provisional DILI risk call (positive) with calibrated probability above the 0.558 threshold, and their follow-up decisions are “hold_for_liver_validation.” The recommendation for each is to conduct a human-relevant hepatocyte concentration-response study measuring cell viability and liver-injury readouts to assess concentration-dependent injury.

Limitations: these are generated proposals, not labelled evaluation cases; binding predictions do not establish efficacy; DILI estimates drug-level liver concern, not dose-specific exposure or freedom from harm; nearest-training Tanimoto similarity is an applicability indicator with no validated cutoff; no conventional toxicity comparator was supplied; and generalization of the DILI baseline to these proposals is unestablished.

plan.explanation: The request proposes drug candidates for human ABL1 and liver-safety follow-up. This matches the supported screen‑generate protocol: generate 20 proposals with GenMol using the imatinib fragment, screen the prepared human ABL1 kinase domain (Boltz‑2), freeze the top two by mean binder likelihood, then run the local human DILI model. No unsupported changes to target, species, mutants, or additional targets are requested.
